calls.head: Crash the net vs. Bombs away
calls.body: The Predators get in close, but the Bruins mostly shoot from distance. Nashville is near the top of the league for shots from in close, and Boston is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Predators to do more of their damage around the net.

calls.head: Where the Bruins have the edge: shot quality
calls.body: The Bruins are near the top of the league for shot quality, and the Predators are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Bruins’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Predators’.

surprises.head: Boston hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Boston’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 25, against their usual 104 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 450 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: A shutout for Michael DiPietro
surprises.body: DiPietro stopped all 28 shots, worth 3.1 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 70 starts.

story.head: DiPietro blanks the Predators
paras: An ugly night for the Predators. Casey Mittelstadt got the scoring started for the Bruins early in the first, and Elias Lindholm made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. David Pastrňák stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the second. JJ Peterka made it 4-0 late in the period, and Mark Kastelic stretched the lead to 5-0 early in the third. Pastrňák scored again with five minutes left to make it 6-0. Charlie McAvoy finished with four assists, and Pastrňák added two assists for a four-point night.

The Bruins carried the play, and got the result to match. Michael DiPietro made 28 saves for his first NHL shutout. Justus Annunen allowed six goals on 31 shots for the Predators. The Bruins improved to 8-2-1, still first in the Atlantic, while the Preds dropped to 3-3-3, slipping to seventh in the Central.
